items.title: Joe Mares Jr. Interview, 1960-04-08
items.q: And all that Austin High Gang, Teshmark and the whole bunch tried to come in and listen to the New Orleans Rhythm Kings.

ctx.x: Millenberg and the... Now the Farewell Blues was made right on the bandstand. After Paul told me, of course, they used to play from seven to seven, you know, in those days, when they played at the Fryers Inn. And all the boys used to come listen to them. Bix was one of the... Every night is there, till they almost had to throw him out the joint. Bix and Benny Goodman and Mac Port.

And all that Austin High Gang, Teshmark and the whole bunch tried to come in and listen to the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. Now, getting back to the Farewell Blues, after a session one time, Rap was looking for some harmonies with Paul, and they ran into the Farewell Blues, and they called it the Railroad Blues, because they had those wah-wah effects, you know, and they called it Railroad Blues, and finally called it the Farewell Blues.

I know when I first met George Brunus, 1936 in New York, I gave him a couple of those Jeanette records, and he said that Farewell Blues is something that Rap worked that out of the weary blues. He took a little phrase out of the weary blues.
